subsystem: cross-chain bridges and universal routing (universal Cross-chain Router flofi.router.universal over Relay; certified BUILD-ROUTER-001 Router flofi.router over Across/LI.FI; discovery-only LI.FI/Mayan/Across quotes; workflow-run consumption of bridge deliveries)
summary: Two bridge runtimes exist and both are owner-signed and owner-gas-paid already. (1) The universal router (flow 'crosschain-universal', apps/reference-dapp/src/server/universal-router/service.ts) executes ONLY Relay (protocol 'relay-depository'): it asks Relay /quote/v2 (EXACT_INPUT), recomputes the Relay v2 orderId from orderData, verifies the order field by field (one input of the exact amount, one payment to the recipient, no destination calls, no order fees, refunds only to owner/recipient, minimum within the owner's slippage, deadline > now+600 s) and rebuilds the source transaction itself (EVM: exact approve + depositErc20/depositNative on the pinned Depository 0x4cd0...bc31; Solana: deposit_token/deposit_native on the pinned program 99vQ...SrN2) requiring byte equality with Relay's. LI.FI, Mayan and Across are asked during discovery only and are labelled NOT_EXECUTABLE in the universal service. Relay covers all 20 directed pairs of Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum/Robinhood(4663)/Solana including EVM->Solana and Solana->EVM (MOCKED tests for all 20; a 2026-10-25 read-only quote matrix shows 40/40 EXECUTABLE quotes; no mainnet transaction was ever sent). The route's guaranteed minimum is the Relay order's output payment minimumAmount (route.minimumOutput), bound into the orderId the deposit carries. (2) The certified Router (flow 'crosschain-router', router-service.ts) executes Across SpokePool deposits (direct or via the LI.FI Diamond) for 12 EVM USDC/USDG directed pairs among Base/Arbitrum/Ethereum/Robinhood with an exact outputAmount (expected == minimum). Delivery: the universal router learns destination tx hashes ONLY from Relay's status API (a hint) and proves each one on the destination chain (EVM receipt Transfer net credit / direct native transfer; Solana finalized pre/post balances), records DestinationDelivery.amount and record.received, and reconciles only when source and destination are final; below-minimum is DIVERGENT, refunds are verified on chain (source or destination chain), no fill after 1 h is RECOVERY_REQUIRED (still observing); there is no order-deadline timeout and no destination log scan. The certified Router additionally scans FilledRelay logs and uses the fill deadline. Workflow runs consume a bridge's record.received via received-amounts.ts only after the step is RECONCILED (observe.ts requires RECONCILED evidence), but never check that the bridge's recipient is the run's bound destination wallet, and a REFUNDED bridge is reported as OPEN rather than FAILED. Source transactions are emitted one wallet transaction per call (approval, then deposit) with per-transaction nonce/order claims and a verifier that accepts only direct transactions or DelegationManager redemptions, so an EIP-5792 batch or ERC-4337 UserOperation carrying the deposit would currently be classified TRANSACTION_MISMATCH/DIVERGENT. Review/quote validity is at most 120 s (and order deadline - 600 s); Solana deposits also expire with their recent blockhash.

answers.question: Q1. Which providers are implemented for real (Relay, LI.FI, Mayan, Across) and for which directed pairs among Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum/Robinhood/Solana (incl. EVM->Solana and Solana->EVM)? Which return a guaranteed minimum usable as a signed lower bound for a dependent step?
answers.answer: Relay is the ONLY provider the universal router executes: selectRoute queries only 'relay' and records the others as NOT_EXECUTABLE with LIFI_BRIDGE_VERIFIER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, MAYAN_TRANSACTION_BUILDER_NOT_VERIFIED, ACROSS_EXECUTES_ON_CERTIFIED_ROUTER; the cloud flow and the server action construct the service with providers {relay} only. Relay covers all 20 directed pairs of the five networks, including every EVM->Solana and Solana->EVM pair and Robinhood Chain (Relay slug 'robinhood'), same-asset and cross-asset (the solver delivers the destination asset). Evidence level: MOCKED end-to-end for all 20 directions (native->native and stablecoin->native) in service.test.ts; a read-only public quote matrix of 2026-10-25 shows 40/40 rows EXECUTABLE through Relay with public quote subjects; no mainnet transaction was sent by that build (report line 17). Across executes only through the certified BUILD-ROUTER-001 Router (flow crosschain-router, adapter flofi.router), never through the universal router, for 12 EVM USDC/USDG directed pairs among Base, Arbitrum One, Ethereum and Robinhood (plus a Base Sepolia test pair); LI.FI executes only inside that certified Router (LI.FI Diamond -> Across V4) for the same pairs. LI.FI (other tools), Mayan (Solana/Base/Arbitrum/Ethereum; no Robinhood) and Across (EVM only, no Solana; ERC-20 only in universal discovery) are discovery/LIVE_QUOTE only. Guaranteed minimums: Relay route.minimumOutput = the order's output payment minimumAmount, checked against the owner's slippage, committed by the orderId the deposit carries, re-checked at delivery (a credit below it is DIVERGENT) - usable as the signed lower bound of a dependent step once the bridge's Review is fixed. Across (certified Router) is exact: minimumOutput == expectedOutput == outputAmount encoded in the deposit calldata, and the fill is checked within [minimum, expected]. LI.FI toAmountMin and Mayan minAmountOutBaseUnits and Across minOutputAmount in universal discovery are display-only quote fields (not bound to anything signed) and must NOT be used as signed bounds. Note: the CHECKPOINT phrase 'Across SVM' has no code support (Across network entry for Solana is null).

answers.question: Q2. How is destination delivery observed and reconciled (provider status API vs destination chain read)? Which record fields carry the delivered amount, partial fills, refunds, timeouts?
answers.answer: Universal router: discovery of the destination transaction is by provider hint only - Relay GET /intents/status/v3?requestId=<quote id>; destination hashes are taken only when status is 'success' (FILLED) and refund hashes only when 'refund' (REFUNDED). Proof is always a destination-chain read: EVM canonical receipt (non-zero block hash that is the canonical block containing the tx), status 1, ERC-20 net Transfer credit to the recipient in the output token, or for native ETH a direct transaction whose to == recipient (otherwise UNVERIFIABLE_NATIVE, the run keeps waiting with UNIVERSAL_DELIVERY_NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIABLE); Solana finalized transaction net credit from pre/post (token) balances. orderBound records whether the order id appears in calldata/logs (informational). The delivery transaction is claimed by exactly one run. There is NO destination log scan in the universal router (unlike the certified Router's FilledRelay scan), so a Relay status outage delays observation indefinitely. Fields: record.destination (DestinationDelivery: chainId, transactionHash, position, blockHash, timestamp, recipient, token, amount, orderBound, discoveredBy 'PROVIDER_HINT', contentHash, final), record.received (= destination.amount, set at DESTINATION_OBSERVED, before finality), record.refund (RefundRecord: chainId, transactionHash, recipient, token, amount), record.lastHint (ProviderStatusHint), record.phase/verdict (PENDING|RECONCILED|DIVERGENT|FAILED|REFUNDED), record.error, evidence.minimumOutput and evidence.received at RECONCILED; the Review keeps expectedOutput/minimumOutput in review.route and orderDeadline in review.deadlines. Partial fills: not modeled - each hinted tx must alone credit >= minimumOutput; the first hinted tx that credits less is DIVERGENT (UNIVERSAL_DELIVERY_BELOW_MINIMUM); a fill split across several txs would be divergent or wait. Refunds: provider REFUNDED -> RECOVERY_REQUIRED (error UNIVERSAL_REFUND_NOT_OBSERVED) -> REFUNDED once a refund credit is verified final, either on the source chain to the owner in the input token or on the destination chain to the recipient in the output token (the order allows both), any amount >= 1. Timeouts: no delivery deliveryAttentionSeconds (3600 s) after source confirmation, or a FAILED hint -> RECOVERY_REQUIRED with UNIVERSAL_DELIVERY_DELAYED / UNIVERSAL_PROVIDER_REPORTED_FAILURE_REFUND_EXPECTED, but the run keeps observing and a late fill can still reconcile (RECOVERY_REQUIRED -> DESTINATION_OBSERVED is allowed); the Relay order deadline is NOT used to decide anything after the deposit. Reorgs of source or destination -> RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED (DIVERGENT). answers.question: Q3. How does a bridge step's source transaction get built (EVM approval+deposit; Solana instruction/tx)? Could those calls be batched with preceding same-chain steps in one EIP-5792 batch or one UserOperation? Does the route quote expire, and how fast?
answers.answer: EVM: FloFi rebuilds the Relay steps itself: approve(Depository, exact amount) (only when the current allowance is short) and depositErc20(owner, token, amount, orderId) on the pinned Depository, or depositNative(owner, orderId) with value = amount; Relay's own steps must equal these byte for byte and nothing else is accepted. The Review simulates [approval?, deposit] together with eth_simulateV1 from the owner, but execution sends ONE wallet transaction per call: begin prepares APPROVAL (if needed) as its own attempt with the owner's pending nonce, then a second begin/handoff/eth_sendTransaction for the DEPOSIT; review.authorizations.sourceSignatures = 1 or 2. Solana: one instruction (deposit_native or deposit_token with every account derived, owner = sole signer) compiled by FloFi into a v0 message [SetComputeUnitLimit, SetComputeUnitPrice, deposit], owner fee payer, recent 'confirmed' blockhash, no ALTs; wallet signs, FloFi verifies the exact bytes and broadcasts once. Batching: technically the calls are plain owner calls with no provider signature or permit, so [preceding swap calls..., approve, depositErc20] or [..., depositNative{value}] can be one EIP-5792 atomic batch or one 7702 UserOperation execute(batch) - msg.sender is the owner's own account, which is the depositor the Depository event records. But four things block it today: (a) the Relay order commits the EXACT input amount (order input.payment.amount == amount, deposit carries amount+orderId), so a bridge funded by a preceding swap in the same batch must be quoted for a fixed amount <= the swap's guaranteed minimum (the excess stays in the wallet); (b) the quote/Review is valid for at most min(now+120 s, order deadline-600 s), so a bridge can only sit in a group submitted immediately (EVM_WALLET_BATCH or SOLANA_SIGN_ALL signed and sent at once); it cannot be pre-signed in a DELAYED group (EVM_USER_OPERATION or SOLANA_DURABLE_NONCE) - after a delay the order would be stale and at best refunded; (c) the service's source verifier accepts only a direct owner transaction or a DelegationManager redemption (and native deposits only direct), so a 7702 self-execute batch (tx.to = owner) or an EntryPoint bundle (tx.to = EntryPoint, from = bundler) would be TRANSACTION_MISMATCH -> RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; reconciliation must instead use the batch/bundle receipt's Relay deposit event + owner debit (assertDepositEffects already works on any receipt's logs) and the group's own receipt checks; (d) Review prechecks the owner's current balance (EVM 'UNIVERSAL_INSUFFICIENT_TOKEN', Solana simulateSolanaDeposit owner token >= amount) and simulates from current state, so a deposit funded by an earlier call of the same group fails Review unless the whole group is simulated together (eth_simulateV1 can take every call of the group in one blockStateCalls; Solana has no bundle simulation on a standard RPC). The per-attempt nonce claim (chain, owner, nonce) and order claim also assume one transaction per attempt. A Solana deposit could join a SOLANA_SIGN_ALL group as its own transaction (one prompt), submitted promptly before lastValidBlockHeight and the 120 s Review expiry. Expiry: deployment reviewTtlSeconds = 120; quote.expiresAt = min(now + 120 s, order.deadline - 600 s) and the order deadline must be > now + 600 s; Review expiresAt = min(observed + 120 s, quote.expiresAt); begin re-quotes the same provider and refuses material changes (ROUTE_CHANGED); Solana also requires blockheight < lastValidBlockHeight. Certified Router reviews last 180 s and stop 300 s before the SpokePool quote-time buffer or fill deadline.

answers.question: Q4. What recipient rules exist (CONNECTED_OWNER, CONNECTED_DESTINATION_WALLET) and how is the destination wallet proven?
answers.answer: IR rules: CONNECTED_OWNER is allowed only when source and destination share an ecosystem (EVM->EVM); CONNECTED_DESTINATION_WALLET only across ecosystems (Solana<->EVM); otherwise an explicit canonical destination address (zero address / System Program refused). Authoring maps an empty recipient to CONNECTED_DESTINATION_WALLET across ecosystems else CONNECTED_OWNER. Binding at Review (bindRecipient): CONNECTED_OWNER = the source owner address; CONNECTED_DESTINATION_WALLET = the destinationWallet argument, only canonicalized (UNIVERSAL_DESTINATION_WALLET_REQUIRED/INVALID); explicit = canonical address. Review records recipientKind and recipientHasCode (EVM eth_getCode at the destination; shown to the owner as 'this address is a contract'). Solana recipients must be on-curve, system-owned, not token accounts. The Relay order must pay exactly that recipient (RELAY_ORDER_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH), refunds may only go to the owner on the source chain or to the recipient on the destination chain, and route.refundAddress must equal the depositor. Proof of the destination wallet: NONE on the server. The server action authenticates only the SOURCE wallet session (SIWE for an EVM owner, SIWS for a Solana owner, chosen by the owner address format) and passes destinationWallet through; the browser fills it from the other ecosystem's currently connected account (EVM injected/FloFi wallet account or the Solana session account) without a sign-in for that ecosystem being required by the server. Workflow runs prove a wallet per namespace at claim time (see maps/workflow-runs.json), but the run never checks that a bridge step's review.recipient equals the run's bound wallet for the destination namespace: observe.ts matches runs by flow + source wallet + workflow hash only, received-amounts.ts trusts record.received, and workflow-sequence.ts / workflow-bindings.ts treat CONNECTED_DESTINATION_WALLET as 'the owner receives'. So a dependent destination step can be bound to an amount that was delivered to a different address.

answers.question: Q5. Concrete plan: make a run's destination group wait for reconciled delivery >= the pre-signed amount; record estimated (quote), guaranteed (min), actual (delivered) per bridge step; handle refunds/partial fills fail-closed. Exact files/functions.
answers.answer: See implementationGuidance (ordered). In short: (1) a pure bridgeDeliveryFacts(record) beside amountsFromOwnerRecord giving {provider, routeCommitment, orderId, recipient, outputAsset, estimated=review.route.expectedOutput, guaranteed=review.route.minimumOutput, actual=destination.amount|null, final, refund, state}; (2) persist it in the step outcome (StepOutcome in workflow-runs/pg-store.ts) and in the delayed group's row (migration 0023 workflow_run_groups: waits_for_step, required_amount, bound_route_commitment, delivery jsonb); (3) a delayed group becomes due only when the producing bridge step is RECONCILED (universal verdict RECONCILED, evidence present, source+destination final), review.recipient == the group's bound wallet, delivered asset identity == the group's input asset, and actual >= required_amount (= the amount the owner pre-signed, <= guaranteed of the reviewed route the deposit actually carried); any mismatch is fail-closed (group CANCELLED with a code, nothing submitted, revocation instructions: Solana advance nonce, UserOp never submitted / nonce key invalidated by the owner); (4) observe.ts maps a REFUNDED universal/certified record to StepVerdict FAILED code BRIDGE_REFUNDED (today it falls to OPEN) and RECOVERY_REQUIRED to UNCERTAIN (already via needsObservation); (5) bridges themselves are never pre-signed in a delayed group (120 s quote) - they are EVM_OWNER_STEP / WHEN_DUE or in an immediate EVM_WALLET_BATCH/SOLANA_SIGN_ALL group with a fixed input; (6) harden received-amounts universal branch to require verdict RECONCILED; (7) add an order-deadline timeout and (optionally) a destination log scan to the universal service, and keep partial fills divergent.

implementationGuidance: Treat a bridge step as its own execution group by default (EVM_OWNER_STEP / SOLANA_OWNER_STEP through flow 'crosschain-universal' or 'crosschain-router'): it is already user-funded (owner's wallet sends/signs the source tx and pays source gas; destination gas is a Relay/Across fee inside the quote, not a FloFi sponsor). Count its interactions honestly: EVM = review.authorizations.sourceSignatures (1, or 2 when an approval is needed), Solana = 1, destination = 0 (types.ts:75; service.ts:305, 328).

Never place a bridge inside a DELAYED group (EVM_USER_OPERATION, SOLANA_DURABLE_NONCE): the Relay quote/Review lives at most 120 s (relay-provider.ts:147-149; action-registry/universal-router.ts:65) and the order deadline is fixed at quote time. A bridge that follows another bridge must be WHEN_DUE (fresh quote, Review and wallet prompt at that time with the reconciled amount).

If batching a bridge with preceding same-chain steps (EVM_WALLET_BATCH, immediate only): quote Relay for a FIXED input <= the preceding producer's guaranteed minimum (amount-out min of the swap); add to the universal service a group-aware Review that simulates the whole group in one eth_simulateV1 blockStateCalls (evm-chain.ts:65-80 already supports N calls) instead of the current-balance precheck (service.ts:275), and a new reconciliation entry, e.g. service.adoptGroupDeposit(id, {transactionHash, groupId}), that reads the batch receipt and runs evm.assertDepositEffects(route, d, receipt.logs, owner) (evm-chain.ts:82-95) and the gas-payer check (user-funded/gas-payer.ts) instead of verifyEvmSubmission (evm-chain.ts:121-144, which refuses 7702 self-execute batches and EntryPoint bundles). Delivery-gated delayed groups (migration 0023 workflow_run_groups, working tree packages/cloud-runtime/migrations/0023_user_funded_groups.sql): store waits_for_step (the bridge step index), required_amount (the exact amount the owner pre-signed, base units, in the delivered asset identity), bound_route_commitment and bound_minimum (review.routeCommitment and review.route.minimumOutput at signing time), and a delivery jsonb snapshot. Signing time rule: the delayed group can be signed upfront only after the bridge's Review exists, with required_amount <= review.route.minimumOutput; if the bridge is refreshed (service.refresh, allowed only before any deposit, service.ts:777-785) and its new minimum < required_amount, invalidate the pre-signed group and ask again.
